title: Variables and Data Types
objectives: Understand how to store data in variables
Distinguish between integers, floats, and strings in Python

body.content: Variables are named containers used to store data in memory. In Python, you create a variable simply by giving it a name and assigning a value with the `=` operator.

body.caption: Variables hold strings, integers (whole numbers), and floats (decimals).

body.title: No Type Declarations Needed
body.text: Python is dynamically typed. You don't need to declare whether a variable is an int or string; Python figures it out from the value you assign.

body.question: Which of the following creates a variable named 'health' with value 100?
body.explanation: Python variable assignment uses the variable name followed by a single equals sign and the value.

exercise.instructions: Create a variable named `score` and assign it the integer `100`. Then print `score` using `print(score)`.
exercise.starterCode: # Create the score variable and print it

visibleTests.feedbackOnFail: Make sure you set score = 100 and then print(score).

hints: Print the variable without quotes around its name: print(score)
